options.name: Elliot Mine Area Dispersed Camping (BLM)
options.locationNote: Approx coords — dispersed area ~1.1 mi off route near Jacumba; verify exact BLM parcel boundary before pitching
options.legalityNote: Dispersed camping on BLM land is legal (14-day limit, pack out everything). Legality depends on being on the BLM parcel, not adjacent private/railroad land — could not verify parcel lines. Heavy Border Patrol activity in this corridor; expect vehicle passes at night.
options.cyclistIntel: Zero facilities, zero water — tank up in Jacumba town first. Only worth it if DeAnza is full/closed; the hotel pools in town are a better evening anyway.
options.seasonalNote: High desert ~2,800 ft — Nov nights near freezing

options.name: Lark Canyon Campground (BLM McCain Valley)
options.locationNote: 4.2 mi off route up McCain Valley Rd from Boulevard (net climb); OHV area adjoins campground
options.legalityNote: Established BLM fee campground — fully legal, 14-day limit
options.cyclistIntel: Cheapest legal roof-of-nothing in the area, but it's 13 mi PAST the Jacumba day-end plus a 4.2-mi side climb. Water on site is NOT tested safe for drinking — carry from Boulevard. Vault toilets, fire rings, tables. Can be noisy with OHVs on weekends; Nov 8 is a Sunday night so it should empty out.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; ~4,000 ft elevation, cold Nov nights

options.name: DeAnza Springs Resort
options.priceNote: Dry tent sites — nightly rate not published (weekly is $155, so figure ~$25–35/night); book via Campspot or call
options.locationNote: 1951 Carrizo Gorge Rd, ~2–3 mi north of Jacumba town via Carrizo Gorge Rd (approx coords)
options.legalityNote: Legal private campground/resort, 311+ RV sites plus dedicated dry tent sites
options.cyclistIntel: Best facilities anywhere near Jacumba: two pools (one heated/enclosed year-round), hot tub, showers, cafe, wifi. HEADS-UP: this was famously a clothing-optional/nudist resort for decades; current ownership's website no longer mentions that policy — call ahead to confirm the vibe before committing.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; high desert 2,600 ft, cold nights in Nov

options.name: Boulevard / Cleveland National Forest KOA Journey
options.priceNote: Tent sites est. $35–45/night — KOA site blocked automated verification; call for current rate
options.locationNote: 2299 Ribbonwood Rd, Boulevard — just off Old Hwy 80 route through Boulevard (approx coords)
options.legalityNote: Legal private KOA campground with tent sites
options.cyclistIntel: 40-acre KOA with showers, store, stargazing area; 9 mi past Jacumba essentially ON route, so it shortens Day 50. Solid plan-B if DeAnza doesn't suit.
options.seasonalNote: Believed open year-round — confirm by phone; ~3,400 ft, freezing Nov nights possible

gapAdvice: No camping in Jacumba town itself — the renovated Jacumba Hot Springs Hotel (44500 Old Hwy 80) is rooms-only, no tent sites, but sells hot-springs pool passes; a soak there then 2–3 mi to DeAnza is the play. If DeAnza's rate or vibe is off, ride 9 more mi to the Boulevard KOA and bank miles for Day 50.

options.name: Green Valley Campground (Cuyamaca Rancho State Park)
options.priceNote: $40/night/site standard (per site, not per person); no hike/bike site at this park
options.locationNote: 3.2 mi off route up Hwy 79 from the Descanso area; 15 mi BEFORE the Alpine day-end
options.cyclistIntel: Pretty oak/creek setting, flush toilets, pay showers. Booking is via ReserveCalifornia but a Monday night in November will have walk-up room. Costs you 15 route miles + a 3.2-mi climb off route, making Day 51 to Encinitas very long.
options.seasonalNote: Vehicle-access camping season runs Apr 1 – Nov 30, so OPEN Nov 9 — one of its last weeks of the season. ~4,000 ft: expect nights near/below freezing.

options.name: Lake Jennings Campground
options.priceNote: Standard tent (non-hookup) $45 Sun–Thu / $50 Fri–Sat (rates effective May 2025); Nov 9 is a Monday = $45
options.locationNote: 9535 Harritt Rd, Lakeside — ~5–6 mi past Alpine along the route toward El Cajon, ~1 mi off
options.legalityNote: Legal established campground (Helix Water District park)
options.cyclistIntel: Hot showers, store, lake views, walk-in tent-only sites available; 44 non-hookup tent sites so midweek Nov availability is easy. Sleeping here instead of before Alpine shaves 5+ mi off the long Day 51 into Encinitas.

gapAdvice: Alpine itself has NO campground (confirmed — nothing legal in town), and Vacationer RV Resort in El Cajon is verified RVs-only ('Sorry, no tent camping' per their FAQ), so scratch it. Nothing under $40 exists on this stretch: Lake Jennings ($45, right on the onward path, hot showers) is worth the $5 over Green Valley, which sits 15 mi short plus a 3.2-mi climb and freezing 4,000-ft nights. A Warmshowers host in Alpine/El Cajon is the only free play here.

options.name: San Elijo State Beach — Hike & Bike site
options.priceNote: Hike/bike $15/person/night (raised from $10 — verified on parks.ca.gov Aug 2026); shared site #94, pay on arrival
options.locationNote: 2050 S Coast Hwy 101, Cardiff-by-the-Sea — directly ON route, 2.7 mi before the Encinitas day-end
options.legalityNote: Official CA State Parks hike & bike program — arrive by bike, no reservation possible or needed
options.cyclistIntel: THE classic Pacific Coast route stop: blufftop over the surf, hot pay showers (bring quarters), flush toilets, market/taco shops across Hwy 101. Registration after 2 PM, vacate by noon; max 2 consecutive nights, 10 hike/bike days per calendar year statewide. November midweek = the shared site will very likely be yours alone.
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; hike/bike is first-come and effectively never full in Nov

options.name: South Carlsbad State Beach — Hike & Bike site
options.priceNote: Historically has hike/bike sites; assume $15/person matching the statewide rate — UNVERIFIED for 2026
options.locationNote: 7201 Carlsbad Blvd — ON route, 3.2 mi past the Encinitas day-end
options.legalityNote: State beach campground; hike/bike arrival by bicycle only
options.cyclistIntel: Blufftop campground similar to San Elijo. RED FLAG: reservation systems showed NO upcoming availability at South Carlsbad as of Aug 2026 — this campground has long-rumored bluff/utility closure plans. Call the kiosk (760-438-3143) before counting on it; treat San Elijo as the sure thing.
options.seasonalNote: Possible full-campground closure in late 2026 — verify by phone

options.name: San Elijo State Beach — standard tent site (fallback)
options.priceNote: Standard sites roughly $40–60/night per site depending on location; reserve on ReserveCalifornia
options.locationNote: Same campground as the hike/bike site
options.cyclistIntel: Only needed if the hike/bike site somehow can't take you (it will in November).

bestBet: San Elijo State Beach — Hike & Bike site

options.name: Doheny State Beach — Hike & Bike site
options.priceNote: Hike/bike area confirmed by the touring community as welcoming; price assumed $15/person matching statewide rate (official pages list only standard $50 / beachfront $65 sites) — call to confirm
options.locationNote: 25300 Dana Point Harbor Dr, Dana Point — ON route, ~22 mi before the Newport Beach day-end
options.legalityNote: State beach campground with hike/bike arrival by bicycle
options.cyclistIntel: Classic Pacific Coast overnight: flat beachside camp, hot showers, staff historically friendly to touring cyclists. Trade-off: stopping here makes Day 52 short (~40 mi) and the final Santa Monica day long (~74 mi).
options.seasonalNote: Campground open year-round; Nov midweek wide open

options.name: Crystal Cove State Park — Lower Moro primitive camp
options.priceNote: Primitive hike-in site, est. ~$25/night/site (unverified — check ReserveCalifornia); listed with hike/bike among its site types
options.locationNote: ~2 mi UP Moro Ridge Trail (dirt) from the PCH trailhead — approx coords; 10 mi before Newport Beach
options.legalityNote: Legal state park primitive campground; reservation via ReserveCalifornia
options.cyclistIntel: Closest cheap-ish camp to Newport, BUT: 2-mi climb on dirt with a loaded touring bike, NO water (haul it up), vault toilet only, no fires. Ocean-view sunrise is the payoff. Only choose this over Doheny if you want the endpoint miles.

options.name: San Onofre State Beach — San Mateo Campground (early alternative)
options.priceNote: Standard non-hookup est. ~$40/site (tent-only loop sites 101–157 may run less — verify on ReserveCalifornia)
options.locationNote: 830 Cristianitos Rd, San Clemente — ~1.5 mi inland off route, ~34 mi before Newport Beach
options.legalityNote: State beach campground, open YEAR-ROUND (verified). NOTE: the other San Onofre campground — Bluffs — is CLOSED to camping Oct 1–May 15, so it is NOT an option on Nov 11.
options.cyclistIntel: Hot showers, drinking water, flush toilets. Really only useful as a bail-out if you're cooked coming off the Camp Pendleton bike path — it leaves 87 mi to Santa Monica.
options.seasonalNote: San Mateo open year-round; Bluffs closed in November

options.name: San Clemente State Beach
options.priceNote: Tent campsite $45–50/night (parks.ca.gov); a hike/bike site has historically existed here (~$15/pp) but is unverified — call the park pass office
options.locationNote: Blufftop off Avenida Calafia, San Clemente — ~1 mi off route, ~29 mi before Newport Beach
options.cyclistIntel: Fine campground but Doheny 7 mi further is flatter, cheaper for a cyclist, and confirmed bike-friendly — skip unless timing forces it.

options.name: Crystal Cove State Park — Moro Campground (developed)
options.priceNote: Non-hookup 'low impact' tent sites — reported range $25–75/night by season; expect ~$45 off-season, reserve online
options.locationNote: Blufftop above PCH at El Moro — ON route, 10 mi before Newport Beach
options.legalityNote: State park campground — fully legal; NO dedicated hike/bike site at the developed campground (only the Lower Moro primitive area carries a hike/bike designation)
options.cyclistIntel: Full-service blufftop camp with showers and ocean views, no hike-a-bike required — the comfort play if you'd rather pay ~$45 than climb to Lower Moro.

bestBet: Doheny State Beach — Hike & Bike site
gapAdvice: Newport Beach itself has ZERO legal camping — the nearest camp to the Day 52 endpoint is Crystal Cove, 10 mi south. Cleanest budget move: sleep at Doheny hike/bike ($15) at mile ~2898 and accept a 74-mi final day, or pay ~$45 at Crystal Cove Moro to keep the plan's mileage. Huntington by the Sea RV Resort (mi 2924.2) is an RV resort — tent policy unverified and it skews expensive; don't count on it. Newport Dunes Resort allows tents but runs $75+/night.

options.name: HI Los Angeles — Santa Monica Hostel
options.priceNote: Dorm beds typically ~$37–60/night in November (rates float; book online early)
options.locationNote: 1436 2nd St, Santa Monica — 2 blocks from the pier finish line
options.legalityNote: Hostel — indoor dorm bed, no tent needed
options.cyclistIntel: The only true budget bed at the finish; big touring-cyclist tradition to end here. Book a few days out — even Nov weeknights can fill. Ask about bike storage when booking (not confirmed on their site).

options.name: Dockweiler RV Park (LA County)
options.priceNote: RV sites roughly $45–75/night — IRRELEVANT FOR TENTS: verified NO tent camping, RVs/camper vans only
options.locationNote: 12001 Vista del Mar, Playa del Rey — on the beach bike path ~9 mi before the pier
options.legalityNote: VERIFIED: LA County rules prohibit tent camping and overnight outdoor sleeping — self-contained RVs/camper vans only. The only beach 'camping' in LA County, but a tent tourer cannot legally stay here.
options.cyclistIntel: Do not route your last night around this one — county rules explicitly bar sleeping outside an RV. It only works if you somehow have vehicle support meeting you.

bestBet: HI Los Angeles — Santa Monica Hostel
gapAdvice: Final day — no camp needed at the pier. Dockweiler is verified tent-hostile (RV-only by county rule), so if Grimey wants a roof after the finish it's the HI Santa Monica hostel (~$37–60 dorm, 2 blocks from the pier, 310-393-9913) or nothing budget-friendly; book it before rolling out of Doheny/Crystal Cove.
